title: Bob Crosby radio show, recording and entering the studios
summary: Jerry Gray's call for the Bob Crosby show led to recording, and a trip with Peggy Lee led to Alfred Newman and Fox, making him a busy studio man.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: And so, I turned that job down. I'm stayin' in L.A. I'm not going anywhere. And I was existing, and I was happy; you know, I'd play with these different bands and stuff, you know. So all of a sudden, I get the call from Jerry Gray to play the Bob Crosby Radio Show, and that lasted for four years. And that's when I started recording, with the Modernaires, during the late Forties, about '47 or something like that. Then I started making recordings, and people started hiring me for recordings.

Then I went to Vegas with Peggy Lee on a vacation type thing, and she at the end of it took me out to Fox, and I met Alfred Newman -- and he heard me play. He said he liked the way I played. And the first thing you know, I was working at Fox and recording. And the next thing you know, I was doing different studios, and the first thing you know,
I was a studio man! I was just busy as a bee. I was what they called hot. I played all over. I played all the studios. They used to feature(?) me...
